You are an expert Indian legal AI analyst. Perform an Ontology-Grounded Judgment Clutter Extraction on the provided judgment/order.

=== LAND / PROPERTY DISPUTE ONTOLOGY ===
**LAND / PROPERTY DISPUTE — INDIA CONTEXT**
│
├── **Parties**
│   ├── **Petitioner / Plaintiff / Claimant**
│   │   * Identity [Type: String]	
│   │   * Proceeding Posture [Type: Enumeration: Petitioner, Plaintiff, Appellant, Applicant, Claimant, Writ Petitioner]
│   │   * Property Role [Type: Enumeration: Owner, Co-owner, Lessee, Sub-Lessee, Licensee, Tenant, Occupant, Allottee, Society, Society Member, Developer, Purchaser, Heir, Possessor]
│   │   * Claimed Right [Type: Enumeration: Title, Possession, Leasehold Right, Sub-Lease Right, Tenancy Right, Development Right, Redevelopment Right, FSI/TDR Right, Rehabilitation Right, Compensation Right, Consent Right, Statutory Protection]
│   │   * Possession Status [Type: Enumeration: In Possession, Dispossessed, Threatened Dispossession, Transit Occupant, Constructive Possession, Disputed Possession, Unknown]
│   │
│   ├── **Respondent / Defendant / Authority**
│   │   * Identity [Type: String]
│   │   * Proceeding Posture [Type: Enumeration: Respondent, Defendant, Appellant, Public Authority, Planning Authority, Development Authority, Revenue Authority, Municipal Authority, Society, Developer, Private Party]
│   │   * Property Role [Type: Enumeration: State, Statutory Authority, Municipal Corporation, Planning Authority, Superior Lessor, Landlord, Owner, Acquiring Body, Developer, Society, Adverse Claimant, Encroacher]
│   │   * Authority / Control Position [Type: Enumeration: Absolute Owner, Superior Lessor, Planning Controller, Executive Authority, Delegated Agency, Record Holder, Approving Authority, Adjudicatory Body, Disputed Authority]
│   │   * Records Control [Type: Enumeration: Land Records, Revenue Records, Lease Records, Planning Records, Society Records, Development Records, Tender Records, No Control, Disputed Control]
│   │
│   ├── **Subject Property**
│   │   * Property Identifier [Type: String]
│   │   * Property Type [Type: Enumeration: Land, Building, Flat, Tenement, Agricultural Land, Non-Agricultural Land, Slum Property, Society Property, Leasehold Plot, Government Land, Redevelopment Layout]
│   │   * Location / Survey Details [Type: String]
│   │   * Tenure Type [Type: Enumeration: Freehold, Leasehold, Sub-Lease, License, Tenancy, Allotment, Occupancy Right, Possessory Claim, Government Grant, Disputed Tenure]
│   │   * Land Use Classification [Type: Enumeration: Residential, Commercial, Industrial, Agricultural, Mixed-Use, Public Purpose, Reserved Land, Slum, Redevelopment Zone]
│   │   * Encumbrance Status [Type: Enumeration: Clear, Mortgaged, Leased, Licensed, Tenanted, Reserved, Acquired, Encroached, Litigated, Unknown]
│   │
│   └── **Roles**
│       * Claimant Role Label [Type: String]
│       * Respondent Role Label [Type: String]
│       * Property Relationship [Type: Enumeration: Owner-Authority, Lessee-Lessor, Sub-Lessee-Superior Lessor, Tenant-Landlord, Society-Authority, Occupier-Developer, Co-owner-Co-owner, Purchaser-Seller, Possessor-Title Holder, Citizen-State]
│
├── **Relationship**
│   ├── Property Interest Relationship [Type: Enumeration: Ownership, Leasehold, Sub-Lease, Tenancy, License, Allotment, Possession, Development Right, Redevelopment Right, Rehabilitation Right, Easement, Inheritance]
│   ├── Governing Instrument [Type: Enumeration: Sale Deed, Lease Deed, Sub-Lease Deed, Conveyance, Allotment Letter, Development Agreement, Redevelopment Agreement, Government Resolution, Tender, Sanction Plan, Revenue Record, Court Order]
│   ├── Governing Statutory Framework [Type: Enumeration: Transfer of Property Act, Registration Act, Specific Relief Act, Limitation Act, Land Revenue Code, Co-operative Societies Act, Town Planning Law, Development Control Regulations, Slum Law, Land Acquisition Law, Municipal Law, Constitution of India]
│   ├── Property Rights Claimed [Type: Enumeration: Title, Possession, Enjoyment, Development, Redevelopment, Consent, Rehabilitation, Compensation, FSI/TDR, Mutation, Injunction, Restoration]
│   ├── Public Authority Relationship [Type: Enumeration: Regulator, Planning Authority, Lessor, Superior Lessor, Landowner, Acquiring Body, Redevelopment Authority, Revenue Authority, Municipal Authority, Tribunal Authority]
│   ├── Society / Collective Relationship [Type: Enumeration: Co-operative Society, Society Member, Managing Committee, General Body, Federation, Cluster Group, Majority-Minority Group, Disputed Association]
│   └── Constitutional / Equitable Relationship [Type: Enumeration: Article 14, Article 19(1)(c), Article 21, Article 226, Article 300A, Natural Justice, Legitimate Expectation, Promissory Estoppel, Public Trust, Equity]
│
├── **Patterns Instantiated**
│   ├── Title / Ownership Dispute Pattern [Type: Category: Competing Title, Defective Conveyance, Sale Deed Challenge, Mutation Dispute, Inheritance Dispute, Boundary Dispute, Fraudulent Transfer]
│   ├── Possession / Dispossession Pattern [Type: Category: Eviction, Threatened Dispossession, Demolition, Encroachment, Trespass, Adverse Possession, Illegal Occupation, Possessory Injunction]
│   ├── Lease / Tenancy / Allotment Pattern [Type: Category: Lease Term Dispute, Sub-Lease Rights, Lease Termination, Rent / Premium Dispute, NOC Refusal, Allotment Cancellation, Occupancy Right, Renewal Dispute]
│   ├── Redevelopment / Planning Pattern [Type: Category: Self-Redevelopment, Cluster Redevelopment, Public Authority Redevelopment, Developer Appointment, Consent Dispute, FSI/TDR Dispute, Rehabilitation Entitlement]
│   ├── Constitutional Deprivation Pattern [Type: Category: Article 300A Deprivation, Expropriation Without Authority of Law, Illusory Compensation, Forced Eviction, Loss of Development Potential]
│   ├── Executive Override / Ultra Vires Pattern [Type: Category: Executive Fiat Overriding Statute, Ultra Vires Government Resolution, Retrospective Policy Alteration, Delegated Power Excess, Statutory Safeguard Bypass]
│   ├── Society / Collective Property Pattern [Type: Category: Co-operative Society Rights, Member Consent, Forced Amalgamation, Cluster Inclusion, Majority-Minority Conflict, Society Resolution Dispute, Managing Committee Authority]
│   ├── Revenue / Land Record Pattern [Type: Category: Mutation Entry, 7/12 Extract, Property Card, Survey Record, Demarcation, Measurement, Record-of-Rights Correction]
│   └── Procedural / Forum Pattern [Type: Category: Writ Petition, Civil Suit, Revenue Appeal, Co-operative Forum, Tribunal Proceeding, Alternative Remedy, Limitation, Laches, Res Judicata]
│
├── **Claims**
│   │
│   ├── **CLAIM 1: Title / Ownership / Declaratory Rights**
│   │   │
│   │   ├── **Issue**
│   │   │   * Does the claimant hold a valid title, ownership interest, leasehold interest, allotment right, possessory right, development right, or other legally protected property interest in the subject property? [Type: String]
│   │   │
│   │   ├── **Elements**
│   │   │   * Right / Interest: Legally recognized property interest. [Type: Enumeration: Ownership, Leasehold, Sub-Lease, Tenancy, Allotment, Possession, Easement, Development Right, Rehabilitation Right]
│   │   │   * Source: Valid legal source of right. [Type: Enumeration: Sale Deed, Lease Deed, Conveyance, Allotment Letter, Inheritance, Statute, Revenue Record, Court Order, Long Possession]
│   │   │   * Breach / Cloud: Competing claim, denial, cancellation, mutation dispute, encumbrance, or adverse action affecting the right. [Type: Category]
│   │   │   * Harm: Loss, impairment, uncertainty, or threatened deprivation of property interest. [Type: Enumeration: Title Cloud, Possession Loss, Development Loss, Compensation Loss, Marketability Loss]
│   │   │
│   │   ├── **Facts**
│   │   │   * Claimed property interest exists or is alleged. [Type: Boolean]
│   │   │   * Chain of title or tenure is documented. [Type: Boolean]
│   │   │   * Possession or enjoyment is established or disputed. [Type: Boolean]
│   │   │   * Competing title or adverse claim exists. [Type: Boolean]
│   │   │   * Property records support, contradict, or fail to reflect the claimed right. [Type: Enumeration: Support, Contradict, Incomplete, Missing, Disputed]
│   │   │
│   │   └── **Evidence**
│   │       * Sale deeds, conveyances, lease deeds, sub-lease deeds, allotment letters, development agreements. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Revenue records, mutation entries, 7/12 extracts, property cards, survey records, city survey records. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Possession documents, tax receipts, utility bills, occupation records, society records. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Maps, plans, demarcation reports, measurement records, sanctioned layouts. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Witness testimony and expert title / survey evidence. [Type: Array/Transcript or Report]
│   │
│   ├── **CLAIM 2: Possession / Injunction / Dispossession**
│   │   │
│   │   ├── **Issue**
│   │   │   * Is the claimant entitled to protection of possession, restoration of possession, or restraint against interference, eviction, demolition, construction, transfer, or dispossession? [Type: String]
│   │   │
│   │   ├── **Elements**
│   │   │   * Possessory Right: Actual, constructive, lawful, settled, or protected possession. [Type: Enumeration]
│   │   │   * Interference: Threat, dispossession, demolition, obstruction, encroachment, eviction, construction, transfer, or denial of access. [Type: Category]
│   │   │   * Illegality / Lack of Due Process: Absence of notice, authority, hearing, statutory compliance, or lawful procedure. [Type: Category]
│   │   │   * Harm: Loss of shelter, possession, access, use, enjoyment, livelihood, or property value. [Type: Enumeration]
│   │   │
│   │   ├── **Facts**
│   │   │   * Claimant is in possession or claims settled possession. [Type: Boolean]
│   │   │   * Respondent has interfered or threatened interference. [Type: Boolean]
│   │   │   * Notice or due process is absent, defective, or disputed. [Type: Enumeration: Present, Absent, Defective, Disputed, Unknown]
│   │   │   * Possession is lawful, unauthorized, disputed, or protected. [Type: Enumeration: Lawful, Unauthorized, Disputed, Protected, Unknown]
│   │   │   * Urgent threat requiring interim protection exists. [Type: Boolean]
│   │   │
│   │   └── **Evidence**
│   │       * Possession records, photographs, inspection reports, utility bills, tax receipts, society records. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Notices, eviction orders, demolition notices, stop-work notices, panchanamas. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Police complaints, municipal records, correspondence, access-denial records. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Site plans, survey reports, occupation certificates, building records. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Fact witness, neighbour, official, and surveyor testimony. [Type: Array/Transcript]
│   │
│   ├── **CLAIM 3: Lease / Tenancy / Allotment Rights**
│   │   │
│   │   ├── **Issue**
│   │   │   * Did the respondent unlawfully impair, terminate, override, or deny lease, tenancy, sub-lease, allotment, occupancy, renewal, NOC, development, or enjoyment rights? [Type: String]
│   │   │
│   │   ├── **Elements**
│   │   │   * Tenure Right: Leasehold, sub-lease, tenancy, license, allotment, or occupancy right. [Type: Enumeration]
│   │   │   * Obligation: Duty under lease, statute, allotment terms, rent law, housing law, or authority regulations. [Type: Enumeration]
│   │   │   * Breach: Unlawful termination, non-renewal, refusal of NOC, rent/premium dispute, redevelopment override, or denial of enjoyment. [Type: Category]
│   │   │   * Harm: Loss of possession, use, renewal, development benefit, rehabilitation entitlement, FSI/TDR entitlement, or compensation. [Type: Enumeration]
│   │   │
│   │   ├── **Facts**
│   │   │   * Tenure document exists or is alleged. [Type: Boolean]
│   │   │   * Tenure is subsisting, expired, terminated, disputed, or renewable. [Type: Enumeration: Subsisting, Expired, Terminated, Disputed, Renewable, Unknown]
│   │   │   * Breach or default is alleged by either side. [Type: Boolean]
│   │   │   * Due process for termination or alteration is disputed. [Type: Boolean]
│   │   │   * Superior statutory authority is invoked to override tenure rights. [Type: Boolean]
│   │   │
│   │   └── **Evidence**
│   │       * Lease deeds, sub-lease deeds, license agreements, allotment letters, rent receipts, premium payment records. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Termination notices, renewal requests, NOC applications, breach notices, correspondence. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Authority regulations, government orders, board resolutions, society records. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Payment records, arrears records, tax and maintenance records. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Testimony from lessor, lessee, authority officials, society officers, and occupants. [Type: Array/Transcript]
│   │
│   ├── **CLAIM 4: Redevelopment / Planning / Development Rights**
│   │   │
│   │   ├── **Issue**
│   │   │   * Is the challenged redevelopment, planning, tender, developer appointment, consent process, cluster inclusion, or rehabilitation scheme lawful and binding on affected property holders or occupants? [Type: String]
│   │   │
│   │   ├── **Elements**
│   │   │   * Authority: Statutory, contractual, ownership, planning, society, or public-authority power to undertake redevelopment. [Type: Enumeration]
│   │   │   * Compliance: Compliance with development regulations, planning law, consent requirements, tender process, rehabilitation standards, and due process. [Type: Enumeration]
│   │   │   * Breach / Illegality: Lack of consent, lack of authority, arbitrary inclusion/exclusion, defective tender, non-compliance, discrimination, ultra vires action, or unfair rehabilitation terms. [Type: Category]
│   │   │   * Harm: Loss of self-redevelopment right, displacement, inadequate rehabilitation, reduced area, loss of FSI/TDR, redevelopment delay, or property deprivation. [Type: Enumeration]
│   │   │
│   │   ├── **Facts**
│   │   │   * Redevelopment scheme exists or is proposed. [Type: Boolean]
│   │   │   * Scheme is self-redevelopment, authority-led, developer-led, cluster, slum, or integrated redevelopment. [Type: Enumeration]
│   │   │   * Consent requirement is present, waived, disputed, or not applicable. [Type: Enumeration: Required, Waived, Disputed, Not Applicable, Unknown]
│   │   │   * Public interest or planned development justification is asserted. [Type: Boolean]
│   │   │   * Rehabilitation / compensation entitlement is provided, disputed, or absent. [Type: Enumeration: Provided, Disputed, Absent, Unknown]
│   │   │
│   │   └── **Evidence**
│   │       * Development control regulations, planning permissions, sanctioned plans, government resolutions, circulars, policy directions. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Tender documents, developer appointment records, redevelopment agreements, project reports. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Consent records, society resolutions, meeting minutes, member ballots, objections, representations. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Rehabilitation entitlement statements, area statements, rent/compensation offers, eligibility lists. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Technical reports, structural reports, feasibility reports, FSI/TDR calculations, layout plans. [Type: Array/File]
│   │
│   ├── **CLAIM 5: Government Action / Constitutional Property Deprivation**
│   │   │
│   │   ├── **Issue**
│   │   │   * Did a State, statutory authority, municipal body, revenue authority, or public agency deprive, restrict, dilute, or override property rights without authority of law, due process, equality, or fair compensation? [Type: String]
│   │   │
│   │   ├── **Elements**
│   │   │   * State Action: Government resolution, acquisition, reservation, demolition, redevelopment, cancellation, refusal, mutation decision, tender, or regulatory restriction. [Type: Category]
│   │   │   * Legal Authority: Statutory power, delegated power, planning power, revenue power, acquisition power, or executive policy. [Type: Enumeration]
│   │   │   * Illegality: Ultra vires action, arbitrariness, discrimination, lack of notice, violation of natural justice, lack of compensation, or absence of authority of law. [Type: Category]
│   │   │   * Harm: Deprivation, restriction, loss of use, loss of development potential, displacement, compulsory association, or denial of property benefit. [Type: Enumeration]
│   │   │
│   │   ├── **Facts**
│   │   │   * Public authority action exists or is threatened. [Type: Boolean]
│   │   │   * Statutory source of power is identified or disputed. [Type: Boolean]
│   │   │   * Notice and hearing were given, denied, defective, or disputed. [Type: Enumeration: Given, Denied, Defective, Disputed, Unknown]
│   │   │   * Article 300A / Article 14 / Article 21 / Article 19 issue is raised. [Type: Boolean]
│   │   │   * Public interest justification is asserted. [Type: Boolean]
│   │   │
│   │   └── **Evidence**
│   │       * Government resolutions, notifications, circulars, acquisition notices, planning directions, authority orders. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Objections, representations, hearing records, speaking orders, minutes, file notings. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Ownership, possession, lease, revenue, and development records. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Comparative treatment evidence, similarly situated property records, exclusion/inclusion lists. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Expert, official, planning, valuation, and constitutional-law evidence. [Type: Array/File or Transcript]
│   │
│   ├── **CLAIM 6: Ultra Vires Executive Action / Statutory Override**
│   │   │
│   │   ├── **Issue**
│   │   │   * Did the State or public authority exceed executive, delegated, statutory, planning, or regulatory power by issuing directions that override binding law, statutory procedure, consent thresholds, or vested property rights? [Type: String]
│   │   │
│   │   ├── **Elements**
│   │   │   * Power Source: Parent Act, delegated regulation, executive power, planning regulation, government policy, or authority circular. [Type: Enumeration]
│   │   │   * Legal Limit: Statutory procedure, consent requirement, hearing requirement, compensation requirement, regulatory hierarchy, or constitutional safeguard. [Type: Enumeration]
│   │   │   * Breach: Executive instruction, government resolution, tender condition, policy direction, or authority order conflicts with statute or exceeds delegated power. [Type: Category]
│   │   │   * Harm: Loss of statutory protection, forced inclusion, arbitrary exclusion, reduced entitlement, procedural bypass, or unlawful burden. [Type: Enumeration]
│   │   │
│   │   ├── **Facts**
│   │   │   * Parent statute or regulation prescribes procedure. [Type: Boolean]
│   │   │   * Impugned action alters, waives, bypasses, or overrides that procedure. [Type: Boolean]
│   │   │   * Action is administrative/executive rather than legislative amendment. [Type: Boolean]
│   │   │   * Affected party’s statutory protection is diluted or removed. [Type: Boolean]
│   │   │   * Similarly situated parties are treated differently. [Type: Boolean]
│   │   │
│   │   └── **Evidence**
│   │       * Parent statute, delegated regulations, development control regulations, co-operative law provisions. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Government resolutions, circulars, executive directions, policy notes, tender terms. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Authority minutes, file notings, comparative treatment records, inclusion/exclusion lists. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Objections, representations, legal opinions, and prior court orders. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Judicial precedents on statutory hierarchy, delegated legislation, and executive limits. [Type: Array/File]
│   │
│   ├── **CLAIM 7: Co-operative Society / Associational Autonomy**
│   │   │
│   │   ├── **Issue**
│   │   │   * Does the challenged action force a society, group, association, or member body into redevelopment, amalgamation, cluster treatment, or governance change without required consent, statutory process, or protection of associational autonomy? [Type: String]
│   │   │
│   │   ├── **Elements**
│   │   │   * Associational Right: Society identity, member governance, consent right, general body control, or statutory autonomy. [Type: Enumeration]
│   │   │   * Procedure: Required resolution, majority threshold, notice, general body process, registrar approval, or statutory amalgamation process. [Type: Enumeration]
│   │   │   * Breach: Forced amalgamation, cluster inclusion, consent bypass, voting dilution, managing committee overreach, or denial of member participation. [Type: Category]
│   │   │   * Harm: Loss of self-governance, forced association, dilution of voting power, loss of redevelopment choice, or member-right impairment. [Type: Enumeration]
│   │   │
│   │   ├── **Facts**
│   │   │   * Claimant is a registered society, association, or member body. [Type: Boolean]
│   │   │   * Scheme affects collective governance or society identity. [Type: Boolean]
│   │   │   * Society-level or member-level consent is required or disputed. [Type: Enumeration: Required, Disputed, Not Required, Unknown]
│   │   │   * Statutory amalgamation / redevelopment process was followed or bypassed. [Type: Enumeration: Followed, Bypassed, Defective, Disputed, Unknown]
│   │   │   * Members objected, consented, split, or were not consulted. [Type: Enumeration: Objected, Consented, Split, Not Consulted, Unknown]
│   │   │
│   │   └── **Evidence**
│   │       * Co-operative society registration records, bye-laws, general body minutes, managing committee records. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Consent forms, member ballots, redevelopment resolutions, registrar records. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Cluster scheme documents, tender conditions, amalgamation proposals, authority directions. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Member objections, representations, correspondence, and meeting notices. [Type: Array/File]
│   │       * Testimony from society officers, members, registrar officials, and redevelopment consultants. [Type: Array/Transcript]
│   │
│   └── **CLAIM 8: Adverse Possession / Limitation / Long Possession**
│       │
│       ├── **Issue**
│       │   * Has long, open, continuous, hostile, and exclusive possession matured into a legally enforceable right, or is the property claim barred by limitation, delay, or laches? [Type: String]
│       │
│       ├── **Elements**
│       │   * Possession: Actual, open, continuous, exclusive, and identifiable possession. [Type: Enumeration]
│       │   * Hostility / Adverseness: Possession adverse to true owner, not permissive or derivative. [Type: Boolean]
│       │   * Continuity / Limitation Period: Statutory period satisfied or disputed. [Type: Boolean]
│       │   * Knowledge / Ouster: Owner knew or should have known of adverse claim. [Type: Boolean]
│       │
│       ├── **Facts**
│       │   * Date or period of possession is pleaded. [Type: Boolean]
│       │   * Nature of possession is owner-like, permissive, tenant-like, encroaching, or disputed. [Type: Enumeration]
│       │   * True owner’s title is admitted, denied, or disputed. [Type: Enumeration: Admitted, Denied, Disputed, Unknown]
│       │   * Limitation defense or adverse possession claim is raised. [Type: Boolean]
│       │   * Delay, laches, acquiescence, or stale claim is alleged. [Type: Boolean]
│       │
│       └── **Evidence**
│           * Revenue records, tax receipts, electricity/water bills, possession certificates, panchanamas. [Type: Array/File]
│           * Maps, survey records, photographs, crop records, cultivation records, construction records. [Type: Array/File]
│           * Notices, objections, prior suits, complaints, police records, authority correspondence. [Type: Array/File]
│           * Witness testimony on possession, use, exclusion, and knowledge. [Type: Array/Transcript]
│           * Limitation pleadings and prior litigation records. [Type: Array/File]
│
├── **Defenses / Counter-Narratives**
│   │
│   ├── **Title / Tenure Defense**
│   │   * Defense Theory [Type: Category: No Title, Defective Title, Expired Lease, Breach of Lease, No Conveyance, No Mutation, Permissive Possession, Unauthorized Occupation]
│   │   * Rebuttal Metadata [Type: Category: Chain of Title, Possession Proof, Payment Proof, Authority Recognition, Estoppel, Legitimate Expectation, Long Enjoyment, Statutory Protection]
│   │
│   ├── **Public Interest / Planning Policy Defense**
│   │   * Defense Theory [Type: Category: Larger Public Interest, Urban Renewal, Housing Stock Increase, Infrastructure Upgrade, Sustainable Town Planning, Elimination of Haphazard Development, Safety, Executive Policy Discretion]
│   │   * Rebuttal Metadata [Type: Category: Test Proportionality, Test Statutory Backing, Test Arbitrariness, Test Discrimination, Test Due Process, Test Compensation Adequacy, Verify Actual Infrastructure Need]
│   │
│   ├── **Statutory / Regulatory Subservience Defense**
│   │   * Defense Theory [Type: Category: Lessee Rights Subservient to Superior Lessor, Special Statute Override, Authority-Owned Land, Statutory Power to Redevelop, Compliance with Parent Act]
│   │   * Rebuttal Metadata [Type: Category: Excess of Delegated Power, Conflict with Parent Act, Vested Rights, Lease Protection, Failure to Follow Statutory Process, Article 300A]
│   │
│   ├── **Consent / Compliance Defense**
│   │   * Defense Theory [Type: Category: Consent Not Required, Majority Consent, Statutory Waiver, Authority Ownership, Regulation Compliance, Tender Compliance, Rehabilitation Compliance]
│   │   * Rebuttal Metadata [Type: Category: Consent Required, Defective Consent, Wrong Regulation, Improper Classification, Non-Compliance, Inadequate Rehabilitation, Forced Association]
│   │
│   ├── **Procedural / Forum Defense**
│   │   * Defense Theory [Type: Category: Alternative Remedy, Delay, Laches, Limitation, Res Judicata, Maintainability, Jurisdiction, Non-Joinder, Prematurity, Tribunal First Instance]
│   │   * Rebuttal Metadata [Type: Category: Constitutional Issue, Natural Justice Violation, Ultra Vires Action, Lack of Efficacious Remedy, Urgent Harm, Continuing Cause, Pure Question of Law]
│   │
│   └── **Equitable Defense**
│       * Defense Theory [Type: Category: Acquiescence, Waiver, Estoppel, Unclean Hands, Suppression of Facts, Unauthorized Construction, Illegal Occupation, Encroachment]
│       * Rebuttal Metadata [Type: Category: No Knowing Waiver, Authority Delay, Bona Fide Possession, Regularization, Public Records Support, Proportionality, Clean Hands]
│
├── **Evidence / Proof Matrix**
│   │
│   ├── **Title / Tenure Evidence**
│   │   * Sale Deed / Conveyance / Gift / Partition / Will / Succession Records [Type: Array/File]

CIVIL APPELLATE, JURISDICTION: Civil Appeal No. 73 of 1950. Appeal from the Judgment and Decree dated the 26th January, 1944, of the High Court of Judicature at Patna (Fazl Ali C. J. and Chatterji J.) in Appeal from Original Decree No. 4 of 1941, arising out of Judgment and Decree dated the 20th September, 1940, of the Court of the Additional Subordinate Judge of Hazaribagh in Title Suit No. 45 of 1939.

[IKWEB-1251841:L120]
S. N. Mukherjee for the appellant.

[IKWEB-1251841:L121]
Gangacharan Mukherjee and A. N. Sinha for the respondents. 1952. October 23. The judgment of the Court was delivered by BHAGWATI J, 110 BHAGWATI J.-The question that arises for our consideration in this appeal is whether prior to the enactment of cite13†section 65-A of the Transfer of Property Act in 1929 a mortgagor in possession had the power to grant a permanent lease of the mortgaged property so as to bind the mortgagee.

[IKWEB-1251841:L122]
One Raja Nilkanth Narain Singh was the owner of Gadi Sirampur and he executed the 1st August, 1914, a simple mortgage of Gadi Sirampur in favour of the Chota Nagpur Banking Association Limited. In 1920 the Bank filed a suit against his son Wazir Narain Singh to enforce the mortgage security and obtained a mortgage decree the 29th November, 1921. The Bank purchased a third share of Gadi Sirampur in execution of that decree the 28th October, 1922. Proceedings were taken to set aside this sale.

[IKWEB-1251841:L123]
During the pendency of these proceedings it appears that the 5th November, 1925, Wazir Narain Singh granted a permanent lease of four villages Nawadih, Koldih, Pandna and Chihutia by a registered Patta to one Hiraman Ram who was the Manager and Karta of his joint Hindu family. The Permanent lease was taken by him in his own name and in the name of his son Chohan Ram.

[IKWEB-1251841:L124]
An agreement was subsequently arrived at between the Bank and Wazir Narain Singh that if Wazir Narain Singh paid to the Bank or before the 16th August, 1926, the sum of Rs. 1,10,631-4-0 the sale would be set aside. Wazir Narain Singh executed the 14th August, 1926, a mortgage of Gadi Sirampur in favour of the Manager of the Court of Wards in charge of the plaintiff's estate during

[IKWEB-1251841:L125]
-his minority to secure repayment of a sum of Rs. 1,47,000 and out of the same satisfied the dues of the Bank and the sale in favour of the Ban was accordingly set aside. The plaintiff through the Manager of the Court of Wards filed a suit the 4th February, 1929, to enforce this mortgage and he impleaded as co-defendants in that suit Hiraman Ram as defendant 20 and his father Dilo Ram as defendant 19.

[IKWEB-1251841:L126]
A final decree for sale was passed the 18th September, 1931, and the 111 Plaintiff purchased Gadi Sirampur at the auction sale held in execution of this decree the 6th April, 1935. Delivery of possession was obtained by the plaintiff through the Court the 16th February, 1936.

[IKWEB-1251841:L127]
Dilo Ram died after the mortgage decree but Hiraman Ram and his son Chohan Ram continued in actual possession of the disputed villages and the plaintiff therefore filed the 16th November, 1939, the suit, out of which this appeal arises, in the Court of the Additional Subordinate Judge of Hazaribagh against Hiraman Ram and Chohan Ram, defendants 1 and 2, for khas possession of these villages.

[IKWEB-1251841:L128]
The plaintiff contended that he was subrogated to the position of the Bank, that the decree which had been passed in the mortgage suit was binding the defendants, that he was the auction purchaser in execution of that mortgage decree and that the Patta -being subsequent to the plaintiff's mortgage thus came to an end and he was entitled to recover khas possession from the defendants. Defendant 2 filed his written statement contesting the plaintiff's claim. He denied that the plaintiff.

[IKWEB-1251841:L129]
was subrogated to the position of the Bank. He contended that the decree in the mortgage suit was not binding him as he was not :a party to that suit. lie further contended that the Patta could not be put an end to by the auction sale of the mortgaged property. The defendant I filed a separate written statement. He denied that he was the Manager and Karta of the joint Hindu family.

[IKWEB-1251841:L130]
He also contended that there was a partition amongst the members of the joint family within a year after their possession of the properties in suit and the properties had been allotted at that partition to the defendant 2.

[IKWEB-1251841:L131]
The trial Court hold that, the plaintiff was subrogated to the position of the Bank. It also held that the defendant 1 was the Manager and Karta of the joint family and that the defendant 2 was fully represented in the mortgage suit, that the decree in the mortgage suit was binding the defendants and that the plaintiff was entitled to recover possession 112 of the said properties and mesne profits from the defendants. The defendants appealed against this decree to the High Court of Judicature at Patna.

[IKWEB-1251841:L132]
The High Court negatived the contention in regard to constructive res judicata which was urged behalf of the plaintiff. It then considered the further contention that Wazir Narayan Singh had, after creating the mortgage in favour of the Bank no power to grant the permanent lease in question to the defendants.

[IKWEB-1251841:L133]
After considering all the authorities which were cited before it, it came to the -conclusion that the question whether Wazir Narayan Singh had got such power or not had to be determined with reference to the provisions of cite14†section 66 of the Transfer of Property Act and the crucial test was whether the lease rendered the mortgagee's security insufficient.

[IKWEB-1251841:L134]
In spite of the fact that there was no allegation in the plaint that the defendant's lease had the effect of rendering the security of -the Bank insufficient, the High Court went into this question and a calculation of some figures came to the conclusion that the lease of the disputed villages in favour of the defendants did not in any way render the security of the bank insufficient.

[IKWEB-1251841:L135]
It therefore held that the lease was valid and was not affected by the plaintiff's mortgage, decree or by the execution sale under that decree and accordingly dismissed the plaintiff's suit. The plaintiff obtained leave to appeal to the Privy Council from this decision of the High Court and the appeal was admitted the 9th January, 1946.

[IKWEB-1251841:L136]
Both the Courts below found that the plaintiff was subrogated to the position of the Bank. They also found that the defendant 2 was sufficiently represented in the mortgage suit. These findings were not challenged before us and the only question which survived for our consideration was whether Wazir Narayan Singh had the power to grant a permanent lease to the defendants so as to bind the plaintiff.

[IKWEB-1251841:L137]
The question whether Wazir Narayan Singh had such power has got to be determined under -the law as it stood prior to the enactment of cite13†section 65-A of 113 the cite12†Transfer of Property Act by Act XX of 1929. The mortgagor's power to lease the mortgaged property was the subject-matter of conflicting judicial decisions.

[IKWEB-1251841:L138]
Relying upon the rule of English common law under which the mortgagor had no power to lease, it was held in some cases that a mortgagor could not ordinarily without the concurrence of the mortgagee execute a lease which could be binding the mortgagee.

[IKWEB-1251841:L139]
In other cases a distinction was drawn between English mortgages and other mortgages and it was considered that the mortgagor in India remained the owner and when in possession could prima facie exercise the rights of ownership inclusive of the power to grant leases of the mortgaged property. The Question was decided with reference to cite14†section 66 of the Transfer of Property Act and it was held that the mortgagor could grant leases which were not wasteful in their effect the mortgagee's security.

[IKWEB-1251841:L140]
This was the principle deduced by Jenkins C.J. in Balmukund v. Motilal(1) from the old case of Banee Pershad v. Beet Bhunjun Singh(1).

[IKWEB-1251841:L141]
This line of reasoning was not adopted in other cases which laid down a different rule, viz., that a mortgagor in possession might grant a lease conformable to usage in the ordinary course of management but was not competent to grant a lease unusual terms or authorise the use of land in a manner, or for a purpose, different from the mode in which he himself had used it before he granted the mortgage. This was laid down by Sir Ashutosh Mukherjee J. in cite15†Madan Mohan Singh v.

[IKWEB-1251841:L142]
Raj Kishore Kumari (3)and was followed in a number of cases. There was thus a conflict of decisions which was sought to be resolved by the enactment of cite13†section 65-A of the Transfer of Property Act which dealt with the mortgagor's power to lease while lawfully in possession of the mortgaged property.

[IKWEB-1251841:L143]

It does not however follow that a lessee from the.

A person taking a lease from a mortgagor after the mortgage does acquire an interest in the equity of redemption and can claim to redeem that footing. But this right of redemption does not necessarily mean that a lease of this character is always operative against the mortgagee.

[IKWEB-1251841:L155]
Merely because a lessee acquires an interest in the mortgaged property which is sufficient to enable him to redeem the mortgage it does not follow that the interest which the lessee has thus acquired is operative against the mortgagee. The true position is somewhere in the middle of these two extremes. The mortgagee is not normally bound by the acts of the mortgagor with reference to the mortgaged property.

Briggs (2) the mortgagor might be considered as acting in the nature of a bailiff or agent for the mortgagee.

These observations of Mukherjee J. point out what was the ratio decidendi of that case. The question of the sufficiency or insufficiency of the security was not really gone into but the Court considered that the lease was granted in good faith, was for a limited term and stipulated a fair and- reasonable rent and it was therefore operative against the mortgagee.

[IKWEB-1251841:L179]
The Court was really guided by the consideration that the mortgagor dealt with the property in the usual course of management and the interest which was thus created by the mortgagor in the usual course must rightly be deemed operative against the mortgagee. ,The case of Banee Pershxd v.

[IKWEB-1251841:L180]
Beet Bhunjan Singh(1) therefore is really no authority for the wide proposition that a mortgagor was not restricted in the management of the property by making a mortgage and that so long as nothing took place,to impair the value, or impede the operation of the mortgage the mortgagor would be well within his powers in making a lease for a term.

[IKWEB-1251841:L181]
In our opinion cite14†section 66 of the Transfer of Property Act has nothing to do with the mortgagor's power to lease the mortgaged property. cite14†Section 66 is a statutory, enactment of the powers of the mortgagor in.possession in regard to waste of mortgaged property. The mortgagor in possession is not liable for what in terms of the English Law of Real Property is known as permissive waste, i.e., for omission to repair or to prevent natural deterioration.

[IKWEB-1251841:L182]
He is however liable for destructive waste is acts which are destructive or permanently injurious to the mortgaged property if the security was insufficient or would be rendered insufficient by such acts. This section therefore has no application to the grant of a lease by the mortgagor in possession.

The only relevant consideration is whether, the mortgagor in possession having the authority to deal with the property in the usual course of management, the lease granted by him can be rightly deemed operative against the mortgagee., The true position has been stated in the following terms by,, Mukherjee, in Madan Mohan Singh v. Baj Kishore Kumar(2)

[IKWEB-1251841:L185]
(i) (1868) 1o W.R. 325.

[IKWEB-1251841:L187]
16

[IKWEB-1251841:L189]
(2) (1916) 21 C.W.N. 88 at page 92.

[IKWEB-1251841:L191]
118

[IKWEB-1251841:L192]
> "The true position thus is that the mortgagor in possession may make a lease conformable to usage in the ordinary course of management, for instance, he may create a tenancy from year to year in the case of agricultural lands or from month to month in the case of houses.

[IKWEB-1251841:L193]
But it is not competent to the mortgagor to grant a lease unusual terms, or to alter the character of the land or to authorise its use in a manner or for a purpose different from the mode in which he himself had used it before he granted the mortgage."

[IKWEB-1251841:L194]
The question whether the mortgagor in possession has power to lease the mortgaged property has got to be determined with reference to the authority of the mortgagor as the bailiff or agent for the mortgagee to deal with the property in the usual course of management. It has to be determined general principles and not the distinction between an English mortgage and a simple mortgage or con- siderations germane to cite14†section 66 of the Transfer of Property Act.

[IKWEB-1251841:L195]
Having regard therefore to the position that section 66 has no application to leases of the mortgaged property, the decision of Jenkins C.J. in Balmukund v. Motilal(1) and the cases following that line of reasoning do not govern the question before us.

[IKWEB-1251841:L196]
While we are this subject we would like to em- phasise that it is for the lessee if be wants to resist the claim of the mortgagee to establish that the lease in his favour was granted the usual terms in the ordinary course of management. Such a plea -if established-and it must not be overlooked- that the burden of proof in this matter is upon him-would furnish a complete answer to the claim of the mortgagee.

[IKWEB-1251841:L197]
If the lessee failed to establish this position he would have certainly no defence to an action at the instance of the mortgagee.

[IKWEB-1251841:L198]
No allegation was made behalf if of the defendants that the grant of the permanent lease was a dealing with the mortgaged property in the usual course of management by the mortgagor, In the absence of (9) (1915) 20 C.W.N. 350, 119 any such plea we are of the opinion that there was no. answer to the plaintiff's claim and the permanent lease granted by Wazir Narayan to the defendants could not prevail against the plaintiff.

[IKWEB-1251841:L199]
We have therefore come to the conclusion that Wazir Narayan Singh had no power to grant the permanent lease in question to the defendants, that the same was not binding and operative against the plaintiff, that the defendants had ample opportunity to@ redeem the mortgage if they so desired but did not choose to exercise their right of redemption, that the execution sale of Gadi Sirampur including the four villages in question was binding them and that the plaintiff was entitled to khas possession of the four villages of which the defendants were in wrongful possession.

[IKWEB-1251841:L200]
The appeal is allowed. The decree passed -by the High Court dismissing the plaintiff's suit is set aside and the decree passed by the trial court in favour of the plaintiff is restored with costs throughout.

[IKWEB-1251841:L201]
Appeal allowed.
